newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemalan woman dies at hands of lynch mob.
newsitem.headline: Guatemalan woman dies at hands of lynch mob.

text.p: A Guatemalan woman suspected of trying to snatch a baby died after a crowd of villagers dragged her and another women from jail and beat them savagely, a witness said on Thursday.

About 100 people stoned the two women and beat them with pieces of wood and a bottle, eyewitness Jorge Castillo, a photographer, told Reuters. The lynching happened outside the jail in the town of San Raymundo about 12 miles (20 km) northwest of Guatemala City.

Castillo said the violence ended after several men grabbed a home-made dumbbell from the jail -- a metal bar with cement weights on each end -- and dropped it on the head of Maria del Carmen Gonzalez, 26.

Gonzalez died soon after being taken to Hospital Roosevelt in Guatemala City on Wednesday night, hospital admissions official Cesar Munoz told Reuters. He said Elvira Caal, 24, in fair condition with scrapes on her head and face, refused to talk.
Lynchings are common in Guatemala -- so far in 1997 at least nine men have been beaten and burned alive by mobs -- but this was an unusual case because women were the target.

It revived grim memories of tourist June Weinstock of Fairbanks, Alaska, who was beaten almost to death in March 1994 by a crowd of Guatemalans who believed she was trying to steal a baby. Weinstock survived but cannot walk without help or talk clearly and must be fed through a tube.
At that a hysterical fear of foreigners snatching babies to sell them or their body parts abroad was sweeping Guatemala. The baby-stealer fear has subsided but clearly has not disappeared.

Police jailed Caal and Gonzalez on Wednesday after several local women accused them of trying to snatch a 3-year-old in the market. Before the lynching the women told reporters they may have angered the local women when they begged money to buy a drink because they were hung over, Prensa Libre newspaper said.

Castillo said terrified policemen hid in the bathroom of the jail while the crowd forced the lock on the cell holding the two women. Local women joined in the lynching, kicking the victims as they writhed on the ground.
